<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אייר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918353_theRebbe_128" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_99_D7_99_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918353_theRebbe_128__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that "a locked garden" is like betrothal, where mitzvos create a surrounding separation from desires (like betrothal), preparing a vessel to receive the inner drawing of Torah (like marriage).</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood based on what is said in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="2">that "a locked garden" is like the concept of betrothal.</t>
    <t s="3">And he explains this based on the known [teaching]</t>
    <t s="4">regarding the concept of "Sanctify us with Your commandments and give our portion in Your Torah,"</t>
    <t s="5">that "Sanctify us with Your commandments" is from the term betrothal,</t>
    <t s="6">for the concept of betrothal is designation,</t>
    <t s="7">that the woman who is betrothed is designated and set apart for her husband, and through this she is forbidden to all the world,</t>
    <t s="8">and "give our portion in Your Torah" is the concept of marriage,</t>
    <t s="9">a drawing down into the innerness,</t>
    <t s="10">to the point that the person absorbs the drawing down,</t>
    <t s="11">to the point that it becomes "our portion"</t>
    <t s="12">(of Israel).</t>
    <t s="13">And this is "Sanctify us with Your commandments and give our portion in Your Torah,"</t>
    <t s="14">that the drawing down through the mitzvos is in the aspect of surrounding [light],</t>
    <t s="15">and its effect upon the person who performs the mitzvah is</t>
    <t s="16">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="17">that he be separated from desires and from all evil attributes,</t>
    <t s="18">similar to betrothal,</t>
    <t s="19">for this that the woman is betrothed to her husband is</t>
    <t s="20">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="21">this that she is forbidden to all the world.</t>
    <t s="22">And through this he becomes a vessel to absorb the light of Torah,</t>
    <t s="23">"and Your Torah within my innards,"</t>
    <t s="24">marriage.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section adds that the analogy of mitzvos and Torah to betrothal and marriage is in two aspects: the manner of drawing down (surrounding vs. internal) and the quality of the drawing itself (Torah's drawing is more elevated and intrinsic).</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one may add,</t>
    <t s="1">that the comparison of mitzvos and Torah to betrothal and marriage is in two matters.</t>
    <t s="2">In the manner of the drawing down,</t>
    <t s="3">that the drawing down of the mitzvos upon the person who performs the mitzvah is in the aspect of surrounding [light]</t>
    <t s="4">(betrothal)</t>
    <t s="5">and the drawing down of Torah upon the person who engages in Torah is in the innerness</t>
    <t s="6">(marriage)</t>
    <t s="7">as above.</t>
    <t s="8">And also in the drawing down itself.</t>
    <t s="9">For the drawing down of Torah is a more elevated and inner drawing down than the drawing down of mitzvos</t>
    <t s="10">[to the point that the drawing down of mitzvos is the aspect of hind-parts relative to the drawing down of Torah],</t>
    <t s="11">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="12">the drawing down of Torah is similar to the drawing down of the drop</t>
    <t s="13">(marriage)</t>
    <t s="14">which is an intrinsic drawing down.</t>
    <t s="15">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="16">that also this concept is hinted at in "and give our portion in Your Torah."</t>
    <t s="17">For in the language "our portion" there are two matters.</t>
    <t s="18">That the Torah becomes our portion of Israel</t>
    <t s="19">(as above),</t>
    <t s="20">and that it is a portion of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="21">for when you grasp a part of the essence, you grasp all of it.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that "Sanctify us with Your commandments" is a preparation for "give our portion in Your Torah," analogous to the mitzvos given before the Exodus and at Marah as preparations for the Giving of the Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And one may add,</t>
    <t s="2">that this that "Sanctify us with Your commandments" is a preface to "give our portion in Your Torah,"</t>
    <t s="3">is one of the reasons that before the Exodus from Egypt the portion of HaChodesh was said,</t>
    <t s="4">which contains several mitzvos</t>
    <t s="5">[that are practiced for generations and are counted among the 613 mitzvos],</t>
    <t s="6">for with the Exodus from Egypt the concept of the Giving of the Torah began,</t>
    <t s="7">and therefore before the Exodus from Egypt they were commanded in several mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="8">which was a preface to the concept of the Giving of the Torah that began with the Exodus from Egypt.</t>
    <t s="9">And after this they were commanded ten mitzvos at Marah</t>
    <t s="10">which was a preparation for the actual Giving of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="11">And more generally it may be said,</t>
    <t s="12">that this that the Torah begins with Bereishis because of "the strength</t>
    <t s="13">of His works He declared to His people, to give them the inheritance of the nations"</t>
    <t s="14">is in the manner of the preface of the performance of mitzvos to Torah,</t>
    <t s="15">for most of the mitzvos are dependent on the Land</t>
    <t s="16">(the inheritance of the nations).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
